topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This section introduces the lecture on cancer evolution and outlines the key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Clonal Evolution Driven by Genetic and Epigenetic Alterations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how sequential genetic mutations and epigenetic changes confer selective fitness advantages that drive clonal expansion in pre-malignant tissues.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Hierarchical Models in Tumor Initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine whether cancers originate from long-lived stem cells or transit amplifying progenitor cells using hematopoietic and intestinal models.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and Inflammatory Influences on Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how non-cell-autonomous factors, including chronic inflammation, environmental promoters, and stromal cells, support cancer cell growth and progression.

topics.label: Experimental Approaches to Study Tumor Evolution and Microenvironments
topics.groupedBecause: This section details modern sequencing, computational, and spatial profiling technologies used to investigate tumor heterogeneity and cell-cell interactions.

topics.label: Synthesis of the Multi-Factorial Evolutionary Model of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This section integrates genetic mutations, epigenetic plasticity, cell of origin, and microenvironmental signals into an overarching evolutionary framework of malignancy.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This closing section marks the end of the lecture and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapy.
